title: Creamy Lemon Chicken Pasta
description: Silky lemon cream sauce, tender chicken, and pasta for an easy weeknight favorite.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add a generous pinch of salt, then add the pasta and cook according to the package directions until just al dente. Before draining, scoop out about 1/2 cup of the pasta water and set it aside.
While the pasta cooks, pat the chicken dry with paper towels. Season both sides evenly with salt and black pepper so the chicken has flavor throughout.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sliced chicken in a single layer and cook for about 4–5 minutes, turning the pieces as needed, until golden on the outside and cooked through. Transfer the chicken to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the minced garlic to the same skillet and stir for about 30 seconds, just until fragrant. Do not let the garlic become dark brown because it can taste bitter.
Pour the heavy cream into the skillet. Add the lemon zest and lemon juice, then stir and gently simmer for 2–3 minutes. The sauce should become slightly thicker without boiling aggressively.
Add the Parmesan and stir until it melts into the sauce. If the sauce looks too thick, add a small splash of the reserved pasta water and stir until smooth and creamy.
Add the drained pasta and cooked chicken to the skillet. Toss everything together for 1–2 minutes so the sauce coats the pasta evenly. Taste and adjust the salt, pepper, or lemon juice if needed.
Turn off the heat and serve immediately. Spoon the pasta into bowls and finish with a little extra Parmesan and black pepper if desired.

title: Smashed Avocado Toast
description: Creamy avocado, crisp toast, chili flakes, and a bright squeeze of lemon.
instructions: Choose a ripe avocado that gives slightly when gently pressed. Cut it lengthwise around the pit, twist the halves apart, remove the pit carefully, and scoop the flesh into a small bowl.
Add the lemon juice, a small pinch of salt, and a few grinds of black pepper to the avocado. Mash with a fork until creamy but leave a few small chunks for texture.
Place the sourdough slices in a toaster or dry skillet and toast until the outside is crisp and the center is warmed through. If using a skillet, turn the bread once so both sides toast evenly.
Taste the mashed avocado and add another small pinch of salt or a little more lemon juice if it needs more brightness. Avoid adding too much lemon at once.
Spread the avocado evenly over the warm toast, covering the surface from edge to edge. Divide the mixture between the two slices.
Sprinkle the chili flakes over the top and drizzle lightly with olive oil. Serve immediately while the toast is crisp.

title: Honey Garlic Salmon Bowls
description: Glazed salmon, fluffy rice, crunchy vegetables, and a simple honey-garlic sauce.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment or lightly grease it so the salmon is easier to remove after cooking.
Pat the salmon fillets dry. Check for any pin bones and remove them with clean kitchen tweezers if necessary. Place the fillets skin-side down on the prepared baking sheet.
In a small bowl, whisk together the honey, soy sauce, and finely minced garlic until the mixture is smooth. Reserve a little of the sauce separately if you want extra glaze for serving.
Brush the sauce generously over the top of each salmon fillet, making sure the thicker parts receive plenty of glaze. Let the salmon sit for a few minutes while the oven finishes heating.

Bake the salmon for about 12–15 minutes, depending on the thickness of the fillets. Brush with a little more glaze halfway through. The salmon is ready when it flakes easily and reaches a safe internal temperature.
While the salmon cooks, prepare the vegetables. Slice the cucumber into thin pieces and shred the carrot. Keep them separate so they stay crisp.
Divide the cooked rice among four bowls. Add cucumber and carrot beside the rice, then place one salmon fillet on each bowl.
Drizzle the remaining honey-garlic glaze over the bowls and serve warm. If the glaze has touched raw salmon, do not use it as a finishing sauce unless it has been cooked first.

title: Greek Yogurt Berry Parfait
description: Layers of creamy yogurt, juicy berries, crunchy granola, and honey.
instructions: Wash the berries under cool running water, then drain them well. If using strawberries, remove the green tops and slice the berries into bite-sized pieces.
Spoon about half of the Greek yogurt into the bottom of two clean glasses or small serving bowls. Spread it gently so the first layer is even.
Add a layer of mixed berries over the yogurt. Use a variety of berries if available for different colors and textures.
Sprinkle half of the granola over the berries. Keep the granola in a fairly even layer so every spoonful gets some crunch.
Add the remaining Greek yogurt on top of the granola, then finish with the remaining berries and granola.
Drizzle the honey over both parfaits. Serve immediately for the crunchiest texture, or refrigerate briefly if you prefer the yogurt very cold.

title: One-Bowl Chocolate Cake
description: A rich, tender chocolate cake with minimal cleanup and maximum chocolate flavor.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9-inch cake pan thoroughly, then line the bottom with parchment paper if available so the finished cake releases easily.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, and sugar. Break up any cocoa lumps so the dry mixture is as even as possible.
Add the eggs, milk, vegetable oil, and vanilla. Whisk until the batter is smooth and there are no visible pockets of dry flour, scraping around the bottom and sides of the bowl as you mix.
Slowly pour in the hot coffee while stirring continuously. The batter will become thinner than a typical cake batter; this is expected and helps create a moist cake.
Pour the batter carefully into the prepared pan. Gently tap the pan once or twice on the counter to release large air bubbles, but do not overmix the batter.
Bake for about 30–35 minutes. Start checking near the 30-minute mark by inserting a toothpick into the center; it should come out with a few moist crumbs rather than wet batter.
Place the pan on a cooling rack and let the cake cool for at least 15–20 minutes. Run a thin knife around the edge before removing the cake from the pan.
Let the cake cool further before slicing. Serve plain, with powdered sugar, or with your preferred frosting or whipped cream.

title: Cozy Garden Vegetable Soup
description: A hearty vegetable soup packed with beans, herbs, and comforting flavor.
instructions: Prepare all of the vegetables before you start cooking. Dice the onion, carrots, and celery into similar-sized pieces so they soften at roughly the same rate.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery and stir to coat them in the oil.

Cook the vegetables for about 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion becomes translucent and the carrots begin to soften. If the vegetables start browning too quickly, reduce the heat slightly.
Add the vegetable broth, diced tomatoes with their juices, drained white beans, and Italian seasoning. Stir well and scrape any flavorful bits from the bottom of the pot.
Increase the heat and bring the soup to a gentle boil. Once it is bubbling, reduce the heat to low so the soup maintains a steady simmer rather than a hard boil.
Cover partially and simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the vegetables are tender when pierced with a fork and the flavors have come together.
Taste the soup carefully and season with salt and black pepper as needed. If you prefer a thicker soup, simmer uncovered for a few additional minutes.
Ladle the hot soup into bowls and serve immediately. Let leftovers cool promptly before refrigerating them in a covered container.
